challenges.name: EV-01: The Anonymous Tip
challenges.description:
Halcyon Ridge University has received an anonymous tip that an exam paper has leaked. You are an authorized investigator.

Using only the pages in this lab, find out **who raised the tip** and **which paper it concerns**.

**Flag format:** `EXAM{memberid_papercode}` in lowercase, with no hyphens. Example of the shape only: `EXAM{soc0000_ab0000}`.

hints.content: The tip has a timestamp. Where else is that time mentioned?
Two forum posts share one timestamp. Which one talks about the module named in the notice?
Match the forum handle exactly. A similar-looking handle belongs to a different person.

challenges.name: EV-02: The Study Notes Image
challenges.description:
The Examinations Office was sent a photo of a study-group revision board. Investigators think the file carries more than it shows.

Examine the image and recover the hidden reference.

**Flag format:** `EXAM{descriptive_token}`

hints.content: Not everything in an image file is pixels.
Cameras and editors store extra information inside the file. A metadata viewer will show it.
Look at the free-text fields, not the technical ones such as exposure.

challenges.name: EV-03: The Group Chat Message
challenges.description:
A chat export from a revision group was recovered. One message is not readable as plain text.

Decode the attachment note and read the message.

**Flag format:** `EXAM{descriptive_token}`

hints.content: The note has more than one layer. Peel the outer one first.
After the first layer you get letters only. That pattern suggests a classic cipher that needs a keyword.
Read the chat around the note. The crew talks about a place and "the same word as always".

challenges.name: EV-04: The Lecturer's Laptop
challenges.description:
A lab computer used by a lecturer account was imaged. Work out **when the exam paper was copied** and **which USB device was used**.

All times in the evidence are UTC.

**Flag format:** `EXAM{usbserial_HHMM}`: the serial number of the USB device that held the copy (lowercase) and the UTC time of the copy in 24-hour form with no colon.

hints.content: Shell history can store a timestamp before each command. Learn how to read it.
Several files were copied that evening. Only one is the exam paper.
Match the copy time against the USB attach and detach events in the system log.

challenges.name: EV-05: The Forgotten Exam Portal
challenges.description:
The faculty's old exam portal is still online. A guest account was left for students:

`student_guest` / `guest2026`

Sign in, study how the portal shows records, and find the **internal review reference** held by the Examinations Office.

Only test the portal at the lab address above.

**Flag format:** `EXAM{descriptive_token}`

hints.content: Look carefully at the URL of a record you are allowed to open.
The portal checks that you are logged in. Does it check that the record is yours?
Record numbers are sequential. Try numbers close to the ones you already have.

challenges.name: EV-06: The Exfiltration Trail
challenges.description:
The network team captured traffic from the lab network around the time the exam paper left the campus. This is the final stage: use what you learned in the earlier stages.

Analyse the capture, find the upload that carried the leaked exam paper, and work out **who uploaded it** and **where it went**.

**Flag format:** `EXAM{memberid_service}`: the society member ID of the uploader (lowercase, no hyphen) and the first label of the destination host name.

hints.content: Not all web traffic uses port 80. Look at the busiest non-standard port.
Some streams are not decoded as HTTP automatically. Follow the TCP stream or tell your tool how to decode that port.
Three uploads exist. The module code you met in Stage 1 tells you which one matters. The people from Stage 1 help with the rest.
